title: Lesson 3 Quiz: Poverty, Social Protection, and Public Finance
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not yet reviewed by a human (admin); do not give to students.

Comprehensive audit: q1 key no longer the only hedged choice; q2 key wording matches the poverty-gap definition; q3 percent-entry instruction; q4 explanation states the static assumption. Not reviewed or approved by a human.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Country M uses a relative poverty line equal to 60% of median income. Over ten years, every person's real (inflation-adjusted) income grows by exactly 25%. What happens to measured poverty?

choices.text: It falls sharply, because real incomes are higher for everyone
It rises, because the poverty line grows faster than incomes
It falls to zero, because nobody stays below the old line
It stays the same, because the line rises with incomes

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Town P and Town Q are the same size and both have a poverty rate of 10%. In Town P, every poor family is about $1,000 below the line; in Town Q, every poor family is about $8,000 below it. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Town Q has a larger poverty gap, so closing it takes more money
The towns have equal poverty gaps, because their poverty rates match
Town P has a larger poverty gap, because more families are near the line
The poverty gaps cannot be compared without each town's Gini coefficient

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Omar's housing benefit falls by 35 cents for each extra dollar he earns, and he also pays a 10% income tax on extra earnings. He earns $2,000 more this year. What is his effective marginal tax rate, in percent? Enter a number only; for example, enter 25 for 25%.

Hypothetical example: A benefit pays $8,000 to a family with no earnings and falls by 80 cents per extra dollar earned. Policymakers lower the phase-out rate to 40 cents per dollar. Which pair of effects follows from the arithmetic?

choices.text: Workers keep less of each dollar, and the benefit ends at a lower income
Workers keep more of each dollar, and the program's total cost falls
Workers keep more of each dollar, and the benefit reaches higher incomes
Workers keep the same share, and the benefit ends at the same income

questions.prompt: Compared with a universal benefit of the same size per recipient, what is a typical drawback of a targeted (means-tested) benefit?

choices.text: It needs a much larger total budget for the same payment size
Some eligible households do not apply, so it covers fewer of the poor
It removes the phase-out, so effective marginal tax rates drop sharply
It sends a larger share of its spending to high-income households
